baseline: Host LTP 20260529 renameat202 (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/renameat202): 10/10 TPASS with -i 10 (the runtest entry's flags), exit 0; 3/3 TPASS with -i 3. The test's single assertion, per loop, is: renameat2(olddirfd, "test_file", newdirfd, "test_file2", RENAME_EXCHANGE) must return 0 with the two names in *different* directories (test_dir/ and test_dir2/), and after it (a) the file that now holds the content is readable and yields exactly the 7 bytes "content", and (b) stat() on the other name reports st_size == 0. Because cnt increments every loop, the roles alternate: on odd passes the content lives at test_dir2/test_file2 and the empty file at test_dir/test_file, on even passes the other way round, so a correct kernel must swap in both directions, not merely once. Per-assertion, the correct kernel returns: renameat2 -> 0 (never EINVAL, since the two directory entries simply trade the inodes they point at); read() -> 7 with the original bytes intact (the exchange is entry-level, so neither inode's data or size is touched); stat() -> st_size 0 for the inode that was created by SAFE_TOUCH and never written. Only btrfs is allowed to answer EINVAL here, and the test special-cases it to TCONF via TST_BTRFS_MAGIC (renameat202.c:121-125) -- ext2 is not covered by that escape hatch. Sibling data point from the same host binary set: renameat201 is 6/6 TPASS, including its case 2 (RENAME_EXCHANGE -> 0) and case 3 (RENAME_EXCHANGE onto a nonexistent newpath -> ENOENT).
failing_assertion: renameat202.c:127-130 -- `if (TEST_RETURN != 0) tst_resm(TFAIL | TTERRNO, "renameat2() failed unexpectedly")`. Under Asterinas with CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/ext2, renameat2(...RENAME_EXCHANGE) returns -1/EINVAL instead of 0, so the test never reaches the content or st_size checks at all. qemu.log: `renameat202: fail (0.011s)`, TEST SUMMARY Passed: 0 / Failed: 8 / Broken: 0, versus host 10/10 pass. The 0.011s runtime confirms it fails on the syscall return rather than on any I/O comparison. kirk reports only per-test pass/fail, so qemu.log carries no per-assertion TFAIL lines; the EINVAL is attributed from the single unconditional rejection on the ext2 rename path (see impl), which is the only way this call can produce EINVAL after sys_renameat2's flag validation has already accepted RENAME_EXCHANGE alone.
root_cause: `<Ext2Inode as Inode>::rename` at kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:213-228 opens with an unconditional rejection -- lines 220-222, `if mode == RenameMode::Exchange { return_errno_with_message!(Errno::EINVAL, "RENAME_EXCHANGE is not supported on ext2") }` -- which fires before the downcast and before any work. That EINVAL propagates straight back out through DirDentry::rename (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:866) to sys_renameat2 (kernel/src/syscall/rename.rs:82) and becomes the syscall's return value. Everything above ext2 already handles the mode correctly and is not implicated: sys_renameat2 maps flag bit 1 to RenameMode::Exchange (rename.rs:43-44) and rejects NOREPLACE|EXCHANGE first (rename.rs:34-39); DirDentry::check_rename_mode (dentry.rs:917-927) already turns a missing destination into ENOENT, check_rename_cycle (dentry.rs:895-915) already adds the Exchange-specific ancestor check, and both the same-directory (dentry.rs:828-840) and cross-directory (dentry.rs:877-889) branches already carry a complete RenameMode::Exchange arm that swaps the two dentries' name_and_parent and re-inserts both. Ramfs implements the mode end to end (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:1152-1161 same-dir via exchange_entry_inodes, 1191-1208 cross-dir), which is exactly why renameat202 is already uncommented and passing in all.txt (line 1261) on the default ramfs workdir and blocked only under ext2 (blocked/ext2.txt:2). So the defect is confined to the ext2 backend. The second half of the mechanism is that the guard is not merely redundant: the Ext2 dir rename it guards, kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/inode/dir/mod.rs:233-289, takes no `mode` parameter at all and is written for move-and-replace only. Its apply_dir_mutations (line 329-408) always overwrite_entry()s the destination to point at the source ino (line 349/364) and then delete_entry()s the source (line 356/374), and its step 4.2 (lines 382-394) decrements the replaced inode's link count and calls fs.remove_inode() when it hits zero. Simply deleting lines 220-222 would therefore make RENAME_EXCHANGE silently destroy the destination inode instead of swapping -- the test's stat() of the emptyfile would fail with ENOENT rather than reporting st_size 0. Likewise validate_rename_invariants step 3.2 (lines 309-324) enforces the Replace-only constraints ENOTDIR / EISDIR / ENOTEMPTY between source and destination, all of which are wrong for an exchange, where trading a directory with a regular file is legal and a non-empty destination directory is fine.
invariant: renameat2 with RENAME_EXCHANGE atomically swaps which inodes two existing directory entries name, and changes nothing else: each inode keeps its own data, size, and link count, neither inode is unlinked or freed, and no type or emptiness constraint applies between the two (a directory may be exchanged with a regular file, and a non-empty directory is a legal participant). It is a rename mode of the same operation as replace, so any filesystem that implements directory-entry rename at all must implement all three modes rather than reject one; if the destination does not exist the call fails with ENOENT and nothing is modified. Two corollaries a general implementation owes: when the exchange crosses directories, each participant that is itself a directory has its `..` entry repointed at its new parent, and the two parents' link counts move only when exactly one of the two participants is a directory. When both names are in the same directory, no link count anywhere changes.
owning_layer: The ext2 filesystem backend's on-disk directory-entry layer -- `Inode::rename` in kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/inode/dir/mod.rs, reached through the trait impl in ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs. This is the correct layer and not merely the narrowest edit: the mode-independent half of the rule (flag validation, destination-must-exist ENOENT, ancestor/cycle checks, sticky-bit permission, dentry-cache bookkeeping) already lives above the filesystem in kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:762-893 and in kernel/src/syscall/rename.rs, and is already Exchange-complete, so nothing needs to move up. What is left is irreducibly per-backend: which two on-disk `ext2_dir_entry_2` records get their `inode` and `file_type` fields crossed, and how the surrounding link counts and `..` entries are journaled. Asterinas's split matches Linux's here -- VFS owns the flag semantics, the fs owns the entry mutation -- so the fix belongs in ext2 and the VFS layer should be left alone. Concretely, `Inode::rename` at dir/mod.rs:233 needs to take the `RenameMode` that ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:213-228 currently swallows, validate_rename_invariants must skip its Replace-only step 3.2 for Exchange, and apply_dir_mutations needs an Exchange branch that does two set_entry_target() calls instead of overwrite-then-delete and skips step 4.2's link-count drop entirely.
linux_reference: fs/namei.c and fs/ext4/namei.c, v6.x. Linux splits this the same way. In VFS: do_renameat2() rejects unknown flags and the EXCHANGE|NOREPLACE / EXCHANGE|WHITEOUT combinations with EINVAL, clears LOOKUP_RENAME_TARGET so the destination lookup will not accept a negative dentry, and then returns ENOENT if d_is_negative(new_dentry) under RENAME_EXCHANGE; the ancestor checks in the lock helpers return EINVAL when the target is an ancestor of the source under EXCHANGE (versus ENOTEMPTY otherwise). vfs_rename() then adapts behavior rather than delegating it: may_delete() on the target is called with new_is_dir instead of is_dir precisely because under exchange the target is being moved, not deleted; cross-directory exchange additionally requires MAY_WRITE on the target inode because its `..` is rewritten; and after the fs callback it calls d_exchange() instead of d_move() and skips the S_DEAD / dont_mount / detach_mounts teardown that a replacing rename performs on the victim. In ext4: ext4_rename2() re-validates the flag mask (deliberately duplicating do_renameat2's check, because ->rename has in-kernel callers such as nfsd and overlayfs that never pass through the syscall) and dispatches `if (flags & RENAME_EXCHANGE) return ext4_cross_rename(...)`. ext4_cross_rename() is the reference for the fs half: it re-checks that the destination entry is positive and still names the expected inode, then performs the swap as two ext4_setent() calls with the file types crossed -- `new_file_type = new.de->file_type;` is saved before the first call precisely because that call clobbers it -- and moves parent link counts only under `old.dir != new.dir && old.is_dir != new.is_dir`, as symmetric deltas guarded by EMLINK. It has no rollback path at all: both setent calls run under one jbd2 handle sized for two transactions, so atomicity comes from the journal, and fast commit is marked ineligible with EXT4_FC_REASON_CROSS_RENAME because replay cannot reproduce a swap. The placement is the evidence: every rule Linux enforces in namei.c, Asterinas already enforces in dentry.rs; every rule Linux enforces in ext4/namei.c, Asterinas is missing in ext2. Asterinas has no journal, so the atomicity story differs -- the existing MultiInodeInnerGuards lock (dir/mod.rs:742-780, MAX_MULTI_INODE_LOCKS is 4, exactly the count an exchange needs: old dir, new dir, source inode, destination inode) plus doing both set_entry_target() calls with no fallible step between them is the closest available equivalent.
other_callers: Within ext2, `Inode::rename` at dir/mod.rs:233 has exactly one caller: the trait impl at ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:213, reached only from DirDentry::rename (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:817 same-dir, :866 cross-dir), which in turn is reached only from sys_renameat2 (kernel/src/syscall/rename.rs:82). sys_rename and sys_renameat both funnel through sys_renameat2 (rename.rs:87-103), so those two syscalls are the other user-visible paths that hit the same defect -- but neither can carry RENAME_EXCHANGE, so in practice nobody but renameat2 reaches it and the fix is genuinely local to ext2. No in-kernel caller exists: unlike Linux there is no nfsd or overlayfs path into ->rename here (overlayfs rejects rename outright with EOPNOTSUPP at kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/overlayfs/fs.rs:530-543). What the fix must not disturb is the other two modes through the same function: Replace and NoReplace share validate_rename_invariants and apply_dir_mutations, so an Exchange branch has to be added beside the existing logic rather than woven into it. Two sibling backends carry the identical rejection and are deliberately out of scope: exfat at kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/exfat/inode.rs:1656-1659 (which is why renameat202 stays listed in blocked/exfat.txt:54 and that line must not be deleted) and virtiofs at kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/virtiofs/inode/mod.rs:461-466. They are the same class of gap in different backends, not the same code. Finally, renameat201 -- the only other entry in blocked/ext2.txt -- shares this root cause: its case 2 (RENAME_EXCHANGE -> 0) is blocked by exactly this guard, while its cases 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 are already satisfied above the filesystem (case 3's ENOENT by check_rename_mode at dentry.rs:922, cases 5 and 6's EINVAL by rename.rs:34-39 and by Flags::from_bits rejecting the un-modelled WHITEOUT bit). So it should go green as a side effect, though it stays blocklisted in this run.
suggested_direction: Thread `mode` down into ext2 instead of rejecting it, and add an Exchange branch to the existing rename path. (1) Delete the guard at ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:220-222 and pass `mode` through to `self.rename(old_name, target, new_name, mode)`. (2) Give `Inode::rename` at dir/mod.rs:233 a `mode: RenameMode` parameter. Its Step 1/2 already do everything the swap needs -- it resolves both the source and the replaced destination inode and locks all four participants in ino order via MultiInodeInnerGuards -- so keep them, but make the `is_same_dir && old_name == new_name` early return at lines 241-243 still return Ok(()) for Exchange (self-exchange is a legal no-op, and dentry.rs:790-796 already short-circuits it anyway). The destination is guaranteed present for Exchange because check_rename_mode rejected the None case above; assert that rather than re-deriving it. (3) In validate_rename_invariants, skip step 3.2 (lines 309-324) entirely for Exchange -- ENOTDIR / EISDIR / ENOTEMPTY are Replace-only, and a dir may legally be exchanged with a file -- and extend step 3.1's `..` consistency check to cover the destination inode too when it is a directory, since its `..` is about to be rewritten. (4) In apply_dir_mutations, branch on Exchange before the existing step 4.1: read both entries' DirEntryFileType from the two inodes' `type_` fields *before* mutating anything, then call set_entry_target() twice -- the source dir's old_name entry to the destination ino, the target dir's new_name entry to the source ino -- via find_entry_info + set_entry_target (or a small exchange_entries helper mirroring overwrite_entry at line 452). Crucially skip step 4.2 (lines 382-394) altogether: no link count is dropped and fs.remove_inode() must never run, since both inodes survive. For step 4.3, when the dirs differ, repoint the `..` entry of each participant that is a directory at its new parent using the existing set_entry_target call pattern from line 400, and adjust the two parents' link counts only when exactly one participant is a directory (guarding against MAX_LINK_COUNT, as link() does at line 178); when is_same_dir, change no link counts at all. Set ctime on both inodes and mtime/ctime on both parent dirs. Order the two set_entry_target() calls with no fallible operation between them so a partial swap is not observable -- there is no journal to fall back on, and both entries already exist so neither call needs to allocate or grow a block, which is what makes that achievable. (5) Verify with CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/ext2; note the runtest entry is `renameat202 renameat202 -i 10`, so the swap direction alternates across ten loops and a fix that is correct only on the first pass will still fail. Leave blocked/exfat.txt:54 in place.
